rationales: Milk is a colloid and is therefore heterogeneous.
Ink is generally treated as a homogeneous mixture in this context.
Milk of Magnesia is a suspension and is heterogeneous.
Sugar solution is homogeneous; both milk and Milk of Magnesia make the question ambiguous.
2 M has the highest concentration among the choices.
1 M is less concentrated than 2 M.
0.5 M is less concentrated than 1 M and 2 M.
0.25 M is the least concentrated option.
[He] 2s¹ is the configuration of lithium, not sodium.
Sodium has the configuration [Ne] 3s¹.
[Ar] 4s¹ is the configuration of potassium.
[Kr] 5s¹ is the configuration of rubidium.
Environmental Chemistry studies chemical processes in the environment, not industrial manufacture.
Nuclear Chemistry concerns atomic nuclei and nuclear reactions.
Industrial Chemistry deals with large-scale chemical manufacture, including sulphuric acid.
Organic Chemistry studies carbon compounds.
Deuterium combines with oxygen to form heavy water, D₂O.
Soft water has low concentrations of calcium and magnesium ions and is not made using deuterium.
Hard water contains dissolved calcium or magnesium salts and is not made using deuterium.
Light water is ordinary water, H₂O, rather than deuterium oxide.
The seventh period contains 32 elements, not 23.
The seventh period contains 32 elements.
18 is the number of elements in some shorter periods, not the seventh.
8 is the number of elements in the first two periods, not the seventh.
Nitrogen in NH₃ has a complete octet through its bonds and lone pair.
Each nitrogen atom in N₂ has a complete octet.
Each oxygen atom in O₂ has a complete octet.
Boron in BF₃ has only six electrons around it, so BF₃ is electron-deficient.
2.1 is the approximate electronegativity of hydrogen, not the difference.
3.0 is the approximate electronegativity of chlorine, not the difference.
The difference is approximately 3.0 − 2.1 = 0.9.
0.6 is not the difference between the given electronegativities.
KCl solubility changes more with temperature than NaCl solubility does.
KNO₃ solubility increases markedly with temperature.
NaNO₃ solubility also increases substantially with temperature.
NaCl solubility changes only slightly with temperature, so its temperature effect is negligible.
At 0.25 M, the solution has the lowest solute concentration and thus the most water for a given amount of solution.
A 0.5 M solution is more concentrated than a 0.25 M solution.
A 1 M solution is more concentrated than the 0.25 M and 0.5 M solutions.
A 2 M solution is the most concentrated and contains the least water for a given amount of solution.
Halogens have seven valence electrons with configuration ns²np⁵.
ns²np⁶ is the valence-shell configuration of noble gases.
ns²np⁴ is characteristic of group 16 elements.
ns²np¹ is characteristic of group 13 elements.
H₂O is not the empirical formula of glucose.
Dividing glucose's molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆ by six gives the empirical formula CH₂O.
C₆H₆ is the molecular formula of benzene.
C₆H₁₂O₆ is glucose's molecular formula, not its simplest whole-number ratio.
A mixture can generally be separated into its components by physical means.
An element cannot be separated into simpler substances by ordinary physical means.
A compound is separated into its elements by chemical means, not physical means.
A radical is not the type of material meant here; mixtures are separated by physical means.
J.J. Thomson proposed a model with electrons embedded in a positive sphere, not electron orbits.
Rutherford proposed a nuclear model but did not introduce the quantized orbit concept.
Bohr used fixed electron orbits in his atomic model.
Planck introduced the concept of energy quanta, not electron orbits.
Ionic forces are strong electrostatic attractions between oppositely charged ions.
Metallic bonding is a strong attraction between metal ions and delocalized electrons.
Intermolecular forces are generally weaker than ionic, metallic, and covalent bonds.
Covalent bonds involve strong sharing of electron pairs between atoms.
